text:
maria.g: noticed dashboard spike around 14:22, but traces show steady connections — feels like a sampling artifact from the SSE heartbeat pipeline
kevin: which metric? heartbeat_success_rate? can you paste the chart link?
sre-jen: seeing small blips earlier too, maybe related to canary traffic pattern
maria.g: heartbeat.success_rate on /streaming (see dashboard link: https://console/redwood/d/streaming/heartbeat) — spikes coincide with canary rollout. I suspect our sampling window smoothing biases short reconnects into 'fail' buckets
kevin: we attached a probe to a couple of clients and observed ~30s reconnect loops that the dashboard marked as failures because aggregator uses a 1m rolling window
sre-jen: we've been doing 1% ingestion sampling since last telemetry change. short lived sessions can fall below sample threshold and make the estimator noisy :thinking_face:
harry: proposal: change aggregator to EWMA / decayed-count instead of fixed-window average so short bursts don't flip SLOs. can we simulate the edge cases? :chart_with_upwards_trend:
ux-lab: small UX ask — console shows an "error surge" toast with no context. if sampling is in play we should surface sample rate and sample_count on the alert so PMs aren't alarmed
maria.g: added a small sim harness, results look promising. quick example of the sampling-config we tested:
```python
# telemetry sampling config (sim)
SAMPLING_RATE = 0.01  # 1%
EWMA_ALPHA = 0.2
WINDOW = 60  # seconds (legacy)
# simulate short reconnects and compute estimator behavior
```
kevin: nice. one more gotcha: we must ensure billing and quota accounting aren't affected by this change. telemetry sampling shouldn't leak into quota events
sre-jen: billing pipeline is full-fidelity, but some console metrics are synthesized from sampled telemetry. we'll add a reconciliation check using edge event counts to validate
deploy-bot: Canary rollout: telemetry-smoothing-v2 started on canary-4 at 12:10 UTC (id: roll/telemetry-smooth-v2)
harry: running ~2h now, no noisy alerts so far. do we auto-promote after X hours? what's the rollback criteria?
maria.g: suggestion: run 24h, check false-alert rate and sample variance. rollback if missed true positives increases >2% or if alert noise reduces but actual error budget use increases
kevin: I'll add a console flag to show sampling_rate and effective_sample_count per route (low lift) so SREs and PMs can inspect during rollout
ux-lab: perfect — PMs will breathe easier if the alert toast links to sampling details. thanks team :thumbsup:
